title: UTF-8 for icons
description:
ImGui labels are UTF-8. To put an icon's code point into a label, encode it. Write

```cpp
std::string utf8(char32_t codePoint);
std::vector<char32_t> decodeUtf8(const std::string& text);
```

`utf8` encodes one code point:

| Code point | Bytes |
|---|---|
| U+0000 to U+007F | `0xxxxxxx` |
| U+0080 to U+07FF | `110xxxxx 10xxxxxx` |
| U+0800 to U+FFFF | `1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx` |
| U+10000 to U+10FFFF | `11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx` |

The `x` bits are the code point's bits, highest first. Surrogates (U+D800 to U+DFFF) and anything above U+10FFFF are not valid: encode them as U+FFFD (the replacement character) instead.

`decodeUtf8` turns a string back into code points. A byte that does not start a valid sequence (or a sequence cut short) decodes as U+FFFD and decoding continues with the next byte.

```
utf8(U'A')      == "A"
utf8(0xF0C7)    == "\xEF\x83\x87"          (Font Awesome's floppy disk)
```
hints: For each extra byte, `0x80 | (six bits)`; the first byte holds the marker (`0xC0`, `0xE0` or `0xF0`) and the highest bits.
